# Electrical Docs


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This site covers electricity on paper and in data, not on the bench. It starts with the equations and circuit theory, works through three-phase power systems, single line diagrams and control, then moves to filters and signal processing, forecasts grid load from real demand data, and ends by asking whether a home battery pays for itself. The newer pages are runnable: each works an example in code and checks it with assertions.

For the hardware side (tools, motors, microcontrollers, switchboards) see [Hardware Tools](https://bthek1.github.io/Hardware_Tools/). For the general forecasting toolkit these pages build on see [Time Series ML](https://bthek1.github.io/ML_Timeseries/).

## Theory

|----|----|
| [Physics Equations](01_Physics_Equations.ipynb) | A reference sheet across mechanics, electricity and magnetism, waves and optics, thermodynamics, relativity, quantum and nuclear physics |
| [Electromagnetic Equations](02_Electromagnetic_Equations.ipynb) | Maxwell’s equations, the Lorentz force, the EM wave equation, field energy and the Poynting vector, Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws, and radiation pressure |
| [Electricity Equations](03_Electricity_Equations.ipynb) | Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws, AC and DC circuits, capacitance and inductance, power, machines, semiconductors, digital electronics, control systems and safety |
| [Network Theorems](04_Network_Theorems.ipynb) | Superposition, source transformation, Thevenin, Norton and maximum power transfer, each checked against a nodal solution of one two-source circuit, and why power systems never run at the matched point |

| [Control Systems](07_Control_Systems.ipynb) | A DC motor from physics model to transfer function, poles and step response, P against PI against PID, Bode plots with gain and phase margins, and a discrete 1 kHz PID with anti-windup |

## Signals and Forecasting

| Page | Covers |
|----|----|
| [Filter Design](08_Filter_Design.ipynb) | Pulling a 5 Hz signal out of 50 Hz hum and noise: RC filters, order and the Butterworth, Chebyshev and Bessel families, aliasing, and FIR against IIR filters, including the cost of delay |
| [FFT Examples](09_FFT_Examples.ipynb) | Forecasting strongly seasonal series with the Darts FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) model, improved step by step by cropping, filtering low-amplitude waves and detrending, then applied to hourly nuclear generation |

## Not Covered Yet

- **No power electronics.** Nothing on rectifiers, buck and boost converters or inverters, which are what connect solar panels and batteries to the three-phase grid.
- **No circuit transients.** RC, RL and RLC step responses, and the switching surges they cause, appear only indirectly through the motor model in Control Systems.
- **No protection grading.** The SLD page computes fault levels, but nothing covers fuse and breaker time-current curves or how upstream and downstream devices are coordinated.
